narrative.overview: Pact pairs an airy sky-tinted workspace with a midnight companion theme. The interface remains operational and precise, but soft lavender, peach, and mint message surfaces give User, Claude, and Codex an identity that is memorable without becoming noisy. Dense actions stay charcoal or pale inverse; Iris blue is rationed to focus, selection, and live state. This is an Operate interface. Transcript, Diff, documents, permissions, and runtime activity must remain readable for hours. Translucency is optional material depth, not decoration: navigation may reveal more of the desktop environment, Chat reveals less, and code surfaces remain nearly opaque.
keyCharacteristics: Pale sky canvas and bone-white work surfaces in light mode.
Midnight-blue surfaces rather than generic black in dark mode.
Lavender User messages on the right; peach Claude and mint Codex messages on the left.
Compact, familiar desktop controls with deliberate color fields.
Solid and pure-translucent variants sharing one component system.
Fully opaque type, icons, code, Diff meaning, and focus states.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Speaker color identifies provenance; Iris identifies interaction; green, ochre, and red identify operational state. Every colored signal also carries text, iconography, position, or shape.

rules.name: The Density-by-Importance Rule
rules.body: In translucent mode, Sidebar is most transparent, Chat is denser, and Diff/terminal/permissions are nearly opaque. Text and code never inherit surface Alpha.

rules.name: The Mid-weight Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Use weight 500 for normal emphasis and 600 only when compact accessibility testing proves 500 insufficient. Product UI never inherits marketing-scale display type.

rules.name: The Legibility-before-Material Rule
rules.body: If desktop content competes with UI content, increase the local surface Alpha before adding blur, outline, or shadow.

dos: Do use the four main-workspace references as the visual target set.
Do implement appearance through semantic Tailwind utilities and per-surface CSS variables.
Do preserve meaningful differences between solid/translucent and light/dark modes.
Do keep text, icons, code, and focus indicators fully opaque.
Do use Lucide React for common product controls and state icons.
Do keep keyboard focus, forced-colors states, placeholders and status/Diff foregrounds readable in both themes; speaker alignment and labels supplement color.
Do expose Project actions on Hover and keyboard focus together.
Do fall back to the complete Solid theme when native material is unavailable or inappropriate.
donts: Don't use whole-window opacity to implement translucency.
Don't draw Project-to-Session connector lines or show branch/Changes/path/count metadata by default.
Don't add a persistent `Sessions` label under an already expanded Project.
Don't use gradients outside Relay's specified edge treatment, 3D illustration, giant typography, or 32px marketing-card radii in product UI.
Don't let wallpaper reduce Diff, terminal, permission, or body-text contrast.
Don't treat Agent color as the only provenance cue.
Don't draw one-off inline SVG icons when Lucide provides the control or state symbol.
